summary:
Moldova's statutes on anti-LGBT harm are comparatively strong for the region, and enforcement is the weak point. Since 2022 hate speech and hate crimes have been criminal offences with sexual orientation and gender identity named explicitly, and the equality law was amended in 2023 to cover both grounds. A 2024 legislative analysis by ECOM, benchmarked against international standards and built on a survey of local partner organisations, still identifies gaps affecting LGBT people and people living with HIV in access to justice and in the operation of hate-crime and discrimination provisions.

The ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 records hate speech as a serious problem with no meaningful state response, a finding echoed in the European Commission's country report, and notes that political hate speech rose during the election period. Amnesty International's 2025 reporting states that discrimination against LGBTI people remained commonplace that year, that freedom of expression and assembly was arbitrarily restricted with impunity for past violations, and that in Russian-occupied Transnistria new legislation prohibits promotion of "non-traditional sexual relations".

Document and presentation mismatches have produced a documented discrimination finding. The ILGA-Europe review reports that a trans woman was denied bank service over a mismatch between her documents and her appearance; the Equality Council confirmed the discrimination and recommended preventive measures.

Custody is the sharpest documented risk for a trans person in Moldova. Ziarul de Gardă reported on 15 June 2024 on Igor Brumarețchi, a transgender man registered female at birth in 1972 whose documents were changed to male in 2007, who served a four-year sentence largely at Penitentiary No. 6 in Soroca. He was held alone for long periods in unsanitary, rat-infested cells in the disciplinary isolation unit, framed as protection, while his request to be moved to the unit for detainees requiring protection was refused. He describes forced strip searches, gynaecology summons over the intercom, staff opening his bathroom door, being called by a female name at roll-call, and says only self-harm and hunger strikes got him heard. The National Penitentiary Administration replied that he was held alone at his own written request, that no rights were violated, and that the discrimination claims were unconfirmed. The case amounts to placement of a trans detainee in the men's system by birth sex, prolonged solitary-style isolation, and refusal of protection-ward placement.

Observatorul de Nord corroborated the same case on 7 April 2025: Brumarețchi, from Dubna village in Soroca district, spent three years locked alone in a cell at Penitentiary No. 6, isolated from other detainees and humiliated by staff on grounds of sexual orientation, which brought him to the edge of suicide. The report states that authorities admit homophobia persists in state institutions and that they are training staff and preparing stricter penalties for discrimination and harassment.

Public assembly proceeds openly. Participants of all ages and backgrounds joined Moldova Pride 2024 in Chisinau, and police deployed tear gas against anti-LGBT protesters attempting to disrupt the 2018 solidarity march rather than against marchers. The judicial branch has moved against local suppression: on 28 February 2013 the Balti Court of Appeals ruled the northern city's "gay propaganda" ban unconstitutional and a violation of human rights.

Social climate remains hostile. An Equality Council study, "Prejudices and Marginalization in Moldova 2022", published in January 2023 and cited by GENDERDOC-M, found that 79% of respondents would not accept LGBT+ neighbours and 60% would not accept them as work colleagues, with a social-distance score of 5.7, and that marginalisation of LGBT+ people increased during 2022.
tangentialFactors:
The legal benchmark used by ECOM is international standards rather than regional practice, so the gaps it records are measured against a high yardstick; ILGA-Europe's Annual Review supplies the regional comparison frame for the enforcement findings.

Election-period turbulence is a timing factor: the rise in political hate speech recorded in 2024 aligns with the electoral cycle, and violence and hostility risk around a visit may vary with that calendar.

Russian-occupied Transnistria operates a separate legal layer, including the prohibition on promoting "non-traditional sexual relations", so risk inside that territory differs from the framework described for the rest of Moldova.

Counter-protest violence rather than state action has been the main assembly hazard historically, as the 2018 Chisinau march shows; the state's response that day was to clear the obstruction.
localsOnly:
The Equality Council accepts discrimination complaints and has issued a decision confirming discrimination against a trans complainant over denied bank service, with preventive measures recommended; the 2023 amendment extends equality-law coverage to sexual orientation and gender identity, giving residents a domestic route on goods and services.

Residents have access to the national hate-speech and hate-crime offences created in 2022, which name sexual orientation and gender identity explicitly.

Authorities in state institutions have acknowledged that homophobia persists and have stated they are training staff and preparing stricter penalties for discrimination and harassment, as reported in April 2025.

Domestic remedies are being used: Igor Brumarețchi has stated he will sue in Moldovan courts and before the European Court of Human Rights, and Ziarul de Gardă has notified the Ombudsman and GENDERDOC-M of the case.

Attitudes of the resident population directly shape daily life for LGBT Moldovans, with two-thirds to four-fifths of respondents in the 2022 Equality Council study refusing close social contact.
outOfScopeNotes:
Outcome of the litigation Igor Brumarețchi announced he would bring in Moldovan courts and before the European Court of Human Rights is unresolved here; no judgment or filing is sourced in this inventory.

Whether the Equality Council's recommended preventive measures in the bank-service case were implemented is not sourced.

Enforcement data on the 2022 hate-speech and hate-crime provisions, such as charges brought or convictions, is not sourced in this inventory; the sources address the gap rather than quantify it.

Entry, visa and document-marker rules for trans visitors to Moldova, and screening practices at ports of entry, are not covered by any source listed here.

Whether the Transnistrian prohibition on promoting "non-traditional sexual relations" has been enforced against anyone is not sourced; the legislation itself is reported, not its application.

The full investigation into the Brumarețchi case published on anticoruptie.md, referenced by Observatorul de Nord, was not reviewed for this record.
